{{Quote|Ah, the Rakata! I'm impressed, Doctor. I thought your expertise limited to science fiction, but it also includes holothrillers.|Conan Antonio Motti|<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>}}
'''Science fiction'''<ref name="Blog" /> or '''future-fic'''<ref name="MS1:BS">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref> was a genre of fiction dealing with the impact of imagined science on future society.<ref name="Blog" /> At the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], future-fic [[Holodrama/Legends|holodramas]] frequently included gadgets that could instantaneously assemble a meal from basic ingredients, a feat that could not be accomplished in real life. The [[Journalist/Legends|reporter]] [[Den Dhur]] watched such dramas on occasion, and [[Gender/Legends|he]] once noted how unrealistic they were.<ref name="MS1:BS" /> In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], during a briefing about discoveries of remnants of the [[Rakatan revolt]], mockingly stated that he initially considered the scientist heading the briefing, Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]], to be an expert of science fiction, but re-evaluated him to be a [[holothriller]] expert as well.<ref name="Blog" />
